turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
From the training set, the highest reproducible p-i-n MAPbI₃ devices repeatedly share several features:

- **ITO on glass** as the transparent cathode, giving good conductivity and a smooth interface.
- A **fullerene electron-selective stack** such as PCBM/C₆₀ with **BCP or Bphen** interlayers, which improves electron extraction and blocks holes.
- A **high-work-function, hole-selective contact** such as **PTAA, NiOₓ, or P3CT-Na**, often with passivating additives or blends.
- **Ag or Cu back contacts** for efficient hole collection, with Cu especially strong when paired with PTAA.
- Spin-coated absorber recipes, sometimes with secondary crystallization/passivation steps.

Applying those patterns to the candidates:

1. **c038** — `SLG | ITO, PCBM-60 | PEI, Au-np | NiO-c, Ag`  
   This is the closest analogue to the very high FTO/PCBM/Au-np:NiOₓ/Ag training devices (~20%). The PEI interlayer should further improve electron selectivity, while Au nanoparticles in NiOₓ can improve conductivity/hole extraction.

2. **c030** — `SLG | ITO, IDTT2FPDI | PCBM-60 | Bphen, PTAA | PMMA, Al`  
   Strong match to the high-efficiency Bphen/PTAA:PMMA/Al training devices (~19.5%). PMMA passivation and PTAA’s high work function make this a very low-recombination hole-contact design.

3. **c044** — `SLG | ITO, PCBM-60 | BCP, PTAA, Cu`  
   Mirrors the best PTAA/Cu training clusters (~18.6–19.1%). BCP gives electron selectivity, PTAA gives good hole extraction, and Cu works well as the anode when separated by PTAA.

4. **c097** — `SLG | ITO, ITCPTC-Se | C60 | BCP, P3CT-Na, Ag`  
   Very similar to high P3CT-Na/C₆₀:BCP/nonfullerene-acceptor training devices (~18.5–19%). The Se-substituted acceptor should maintain good electron transport/passivation, and P3CT-Na/Ag is a strong hole-collecting combination.

5. **c058** — `SLG | ITO, C60; PDI | BCP, P3CT-Na, Ag`  
   Another strong C₆₀/BCP/PDI electron-selective stack paired with high-work-function P3CT-Na and Ag. It is close to training devices in the ~18–19% range and has better contact selectivity than many PEDOT:PSS-only candidates.

Final: c038, c030, c044, c097, c058
